# Repository instructions

## Working from GitHub issues

When implementing a GitHub issue:

1. Read the complete issue before making changes.
2. Treat the issue requirements and acceptance criteria as the source of scope.
3. Do not make unrelated changes.
4. Verify each acceptance criterion before marking it complete.
5. Update completed acceptance criteria from `- [ ]` to `- [x]`.
6. Do not mark a criterion complete if it has not been verified.
7. Run all applicable tests, builds, linting, and validation checks.
8. Document any criterion that cannot be completed or verified.
9. Create a pull request linked to the issue.
10. Summarise the implementation and test results in the pull request.

## Development expectations

- Follow the existing repository structure and coding conventions.
- Prefer established implementation patterns already present in the repository.
- Do not introduce credentials, secrets, or environment-specific values.
- Add or update tests for changed behaviour.
- Keep changes focused on the assigned issue.
- Record assumptions, limitations, and follow-up work in the pull request.
